# Daniel Ari Friedman, PhD

I study how systems make sense of the world, from harvester ant colonies to models of Active Inference and the ways people share and evaluate information. I build open-source research tools, teach biology, and draw in pen and ink.

[Research website](https://danielarifriedman.com/) · [Search the catalog](https://danielarifriedman.com/search.html) · [Publications](https://danielarifriedman.com/publications.html) · [Software](https://danielarifriedman.com/software.html)

<details>
<summary>About me and my teaching</summary>

I studied collective behavior in harvester ants for my PhD at Stanford and continued that research as an NSF postdoctoral fellow at UC Davis. I co-founded the [Active Inference Institute](https://activeinference.org/) and serve as its president. I contributed three drawings to [Curio Cards](https://curio.cards/artist/danielfriedman/) and write about William Blake and Buckminster Fuller.

- **Educator** · I teach through the [AII Textbook Group](https://activeinference.org/), with nine completed cohorts on [Parr, Pezzulo & Friston’s 2022 textbook](https://direct.mit.edu/books/oa-monograph/5299/Active-InferenceThe-Free-Energy-Principle-in-Mind) and a first cohort on [Namjoshi’s 2026 Fundamentals](https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262050951/fundamentals-of-active-inference/). At College of the Redwoods I taught [BIOL-1](https://github.com/docxology/biol-1) at Pelican Bay in Spring and Fall 2026 and [BIOL-8 Human Biology](https://github.com/docxology/biol-8) in Spring 2026. Find the livestreams, courses, and workshops in the [media archive](https://danielarifriedman.com/media.html).
